name: Bilbo Why Shouldn't I Keep It
aka: After All, Why Not? Why Shouldn't I Keep It?
look: Two stacked close-ups from The Lord of the Rings: Ian Holm as an elderly Bilbo Baggins, with curly gray hair and a red waistcoat, looks down at a small gold ring between his fingers. Top: he smiles softly. Bottom: he purses his lips into a stubborn, possessive frown.
use: For clinging to something you should probably give up. The top shows the thing or the excuse, and the bottom is Bilbo's possessive turn, often captioned 'why shouldn't I keep it?', for hoarding, borrowing forever or holding a grudge.
slots: top panel: the thing you're tempted to keep, or 'after all, why not?'
bottom panel: the stubborn decision, like 'why shouldn't I keep it?'
examples: Me after borrowing my sister's hoodie
The pen I borrowed in the meeting
After all, why not? Why shouldn't I keep it?
describe: old hobbit smiling then frowning at the ring in his hand
bilbo staring at the ring and deciding to keep it
old man with curly gray hair looking at a ring possessively
lord of the rings hobbit getting greedy over a gold ring
elderly man smiles at something in his fingers then pouts stubbornly
origin: Ian Holm as Bilbo Baggins in The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring (2001), unwilling to give up the Ring.
